notes: Version 2.7 corrects one remark. Version 2.6 described non-trivial holonomy as the minimal structural condition for a gauge symmetry to arise as a descriptive invariance. That is false: the product connection on a trivial bundle with non-trivial fibres has trivial holonomy and still admits non-trivial gauge transformations, and non-trivial holonomy, a property of the supplied connection, does not make the bundle topologically non-trivial. The remark now keeps only the white-paper result that, in the principal-bundle setting, an injective admissible projection has a trivial structure group and hence trivial holonomy, so that non-trivial holonomy requires non-injectivity. The remark no longer attributes to the white paper a non-contractible loop produced by admissibility constraints. No other statement changes.
